description:
GençTek_Salvo Dynamics, tamamı GençTek Gaziantep bünyesinde yetişmiş, uzay ve havacılık dâhil pek çok teknik ve sosyal alanda kendini kanıtlamış 6 kişilik tam kadro bir takımdır.

Ekibimiz; ileri düzey yazılım geliştirme, yenilikçi UI/UX tasarımı, güçlü analiz yeteneği ve üst seviye sunum ile teknik aktarım teknikleriyle multidisipliner bir yetkinliğe sahiptir. Hemen her alandaki esnek ve hızlı çözüm üretme becerimiz sayesinde projeleri fikirden çalışan ürün aşamasına eksiksiz taşıyabiliyoruz.
summary:
SalvoCare is an offline-capable astronaut health and clinical decision-support system built for deep-space missions where communication with Earth is delayed or lost (such as behind the Moon or on transit to Mars).

It connects two interfaces: a Mission Control web dashboard tracking crew vitals, radiation dose, and cabin CO2/O2 via a transparent rule-based risk engine, and an Android app featuring one-tap symptom reporting, context-aware medical advice, an offline space-crop disease guide, and a two-way crew-to-crew SOS alert system.

When cloud AI is unreachable, SalvoCare’s onboard rule engine continues operating using live local data—such as cross-referencing headaches with cabin CO2 levels. Powered by NASA open datasets (DONKI, EONET, POWER, OSDR Inspiration4 data, and NASA-STD-3001 radiation limits), SalvoCare enables faster autonomous medical response in space as well as in isolated terrestrial environments like Antarctic stations, mines, and offshore platforms.
details: SalvoCare: An astronaut health system that keeps working when the link to Earth is lost. What it does & how it works: On deep-space missions, communication with Earth can disappear for long stretches (e.g., ~40 minutes behind the Moon during Artemis II, or up to 22 minutes one-way to Mars). SalvoCare gives the crew a decision-support system independent of Earth links through two connected platforms: - Mission Control Dashboard (Web): Streams every crew member’s heart rate, SpO2, mood, sleep, radiation dose, and cabin CO2/O2. Each astronaut card turns green, amber, or red automatically via a transparent rule-based risk engine (e.g., heart rate > 100 → +2 “tachycardia”, SpO2 < 94% → +3 “hypoxia”; 3+ points = warning, 5+ = critical). - Astronaut Mobile App (Android): Provides personal health status, one-tap symptom reporting with instant advice, an AI assistant, an offline plant-disease guide for space-grown crops, and an SOS button on every screen. What makes it different: - Works offline: When cloud AI is unreachable, an onboard rule-based engine keeps answering with live local data. - Context-aware: Symptoms are evaluated alongside environmental telemetry (e.g., interpreting a headache together with cabin CO2 levels). - Two-way SOS: Triggers a full-screen audible alarm at Mission Control and an emergency alert on every other crew member’s phone so the nearest help—the crew itself—can respond immediately. NASA data in action: Live solar flare and geomagnetic storm data (DONKI) help schedule spacewalks in lowest-risk windows. EONET and POWER track environmental conditions. Inspiration4 data from OSDR and NASA HRP findings serve as references for bone, muscle, and SANS risk, while personal cancer-risk estimates are modeled against the NASA-STD-3001 600 mSv career limit. Benefits & impact: Enables earlier detection of medical issues, faster crew response, and reduced Earth dependency during blackouts. Beyond spaceflight, the architecture applies directly to isolated terrestrial teams in Antarctic stations, deep mines, and offshore platforms. Tools & technologies: Python and FastAPI (backend), Streamlit (dashboard), Kotlin with Jetpack Compose and Retrofit (Android), Google Gemini API (online assistant), and NASA open APIs. Factors considered & limitations: We accounted for communication latency, explainable rules over black-box alerts, crew-to-crew emergency workflows, radiation limits, and hardware feasibility (an 11-sensor smart suit concept where 10 sensor types have spaceflight heritage). Current limitations: Vital signs are simulated in this prototype, the smart suit is a design concept, and the cancer-risk model is a simplified estimate.
